**Weekly Brief TL;DR — 2026-W45 (week ended Fri 2026-11-06)**

**Week:** Mon Nov 2 → Fri Nov 6, 5 sessions · **Basis:** Fri Oct 30 close → Fri Nov 6 close · **Forward week:** Nov 9–13

**Top 5**

- **The AI trade broke on politics.** Democrats took the House and Senate on Nov 3, and newly elected governors in data-centre-heavy states campaigned on slowing construction.
- Thursday Nov 5 priced that into capex:
- **S&P 500 −4.4%, Nasdaq −5.5%, SOX −12%, NDX −6.4%** (worst Nasdaq day since March 2020), ~**$3trn of market value** gone, Mag-7 **−$1trn**, NVDA **−$440bn**.

- **Friday was a bounce, not a reversal.** S&P +0.3%, Nasdaq +1.1%, Dow −0.5%.
- All three majors still fell on the week — a **fourth straight weekly loss** — and the Nasdaq closed in **correction territory**.

- **The fracture is inside the market.** Week: **S&P −2.7%, Nasdaq −3.4%, Dow −0.9%, Russell 2000 −2.1%, VIX 19.42 → 25.64 (+32%)**.
- Energy worst (**XLE −12.0%**, WTI **−12.8%** to $90.83 on US–Iran diplomacy); technology worst among large caps (**XLK −8.2%**, **SMH −11.2%**); defensives positive (**XLRE +1.9%, XLY +1.9%, XLF +1.2%, XLP +0.7%**).

- **The labour report fought the political one.** October payrolls **+165k vs a 65k consensus**, unemployment **4.1%**, AHE +3.1% y/y → **December hike odds ~67% → ~77%** (CME FedWatch).
- Yet the 10-year still fell **7bp to 4.86%** and gold rose **+4.5%**. Daly, Hammack, Barkin, Williams and Logan all leaned hawkish; Chair Warsh has declined to guide.

- **Next week is the audit.** **CPI Tue 08:30, PPI Fri 08:30**; CoreWeave Tue; **Cisco and Applied Materials Thu**; ~a dozen Fed speakers in five days.
- Consensus is split — FactSet 3.9% y/y headline vs the Cleveland Fed nowcast at 3.7% headline / 2.5% core.
